defect_basis.source: frozen allocation table only; no held-out outcomes used
defect_basis.conclusion: a three-stratum deficiency model is structurally infeasible because code is never below equal allocation

hypothesis: Among the only deficiency strata that can occur under the frozen candidate set—structured and technical_prose—residual marginal-learning-value error may be conditioned on the deprived domain. Keep GLOBAL_BASE6 byte-identical and add exactly two training-only scalar mean-residual offsets keyed by the feasible deficiency domain.

frozen_design.deficiency_domain: largest positive equal-allocation-minus-candidate delta over feasible domains; ties structured then technical_prose
frozen_design.offsets: exactly one arithmetic-mean (actual allocation advantage minus GLOBAL_BASE6 predicted advantage) scalar per feasible deficiency domain over training non-equal cases

classification_rules.supported: valid and feasible-deficiency sign-error improvement>=0.10 with MAE ratio<=1.00
classification_rules.mixed: valid, support false, but feasible-deficiency sign error and MAE are both lower than GLOBAL_BASE6
classification_rules.negative: valid and neither supported nor mixed
classification_rules.invalid: any frozen identity, GLOBAL_BASE6 identity, feasible-domain rule, exactly two scalar residual offsets, R30 exclusion, held-out ordering, provenance or accounting rule fails
